issues.description: The Ride class constructor signature is inconsistent with the UML/specification: the problem statement requires a constructor that accepts both attributes (name: String, abbreviation: char) in that order. The template Ride.java is empty (no constructor), and the solution's Ride implementation only defines Ride(String name) (it sets abbreviation to a default), while subclasses (RollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) in the solution call super(name, abbreviation) or assume a Ride(String, char) constructor. This mismatch prevents following the UML-required constructor ordering and will confuse or block students implementing subclass constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Define Ride's public constructor to accept both attributes in the UML order: public Ride(String name, char abbreviation) { this.name = name; this.abbreviation = abbreviation; }. Update the template Ride.java accordingly so students implement the correct signature, and ensure subclasses call super(name, abbreviation) as required by the specification.
